description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 1 on t/op/eval.t's
one-row shortfall).

perl's `t/test.pl`:

    sub tempfile {
        my $try_prefix = (-d "t" ? "t/" : "")."tmp_"._num_to_alpha($$);
        ... return $try;          # a CWD-RELATIVE name, e.g. "tmp_abcd_a"

PCL's transpilable stub `perl-tests/t/test.pl:722`:

    my $try = "/tmp/pcl-test-$$-$tempfile_counter";
    ... return $try;              # an ABSOLUTE path

So every caller that composes the name with a path prefix gets nonsense.
MEASURED in `t/op/eval.t:45-51`:

    my $tempfile = tempfile();
    open(try,'>',$tempfile); print try 'print "ok $curr_test\n";',"\n"; close try;
    do "./$tempfile"; print $@;

`do "./$tempfile"` becomes `do ".//tmp/pcl-test-1234-1"`, which does not
exist; `do` fails quietly (a read failure sets `$!`, not `$@`, so
`print $@` prints nothing), and the file's row 14 is never produced.  That
is the WHOLE of t/op/eval.t's blessed 1-row shortfall.

PROBED: `probes/p3.pl` writes the same program through a bareword handle to a
RELATIVE name and `do`s it, and PCL and perl 5.40.3 agree byte for byte â so
`do`, the bareword handle and the write are all right, and the divergence is
the NAME.

BLAST RADIUS, measured on perl 5.40.3's t/: 50 files call `tempfile()`;
3 compose it as `"./$file"` (`t/op/eval.t`, `t/re/substT.t`,
`t/re/subst_wamp.t` -- the last two use their own `$file`).  perl's own
`$::tempfile_regex` (test.pl's comment: "if you change the format returned by
tempfile() you MUST change the $::tempfile_regex define above") is a second
consumer of the SHAPE, so a file that greps its own diagnostics for the
temp-file name is a third way this bites.

SHAPE: return perl's own spelling -- a name in the CURRENT DIRECTORY,
`t/`-prefixed when a `t` directory exists -- and keep the existing %tempfiles
bookkeeping and unlink_all/unlink_tempfiles.  The companion runs with CWD =
the shadow t/, which is a fresh tempdir, so a CWD-relative name is as
disposable as the /tmp one.

BAR: this is a HARNESS change (`perl-tests/t/test.pl`), so the
WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN table's harness row applies: full sweep + companion
`--all --quick`, both populations, baselines edited row by row.
subject: the harness stub's tempfile() returns an ABSOLUTE /tmp path where perl's t/test.pl returns a CWD-relative name -- `do "./$tempfile"` reads nothing
